reports.note: A tornado carved a narrow southwest-to-northeast path through Keyes, beginning near Phillips Avenue and dissipating past Monroe Avenue. Along the way, it shifted an anchored mobile home, hurled an empty grain silo roughly 100 yards, and snapped utility poles and trees. The most severe destruction occurred near Polk Street, collapsing an old pool hall and tearing the roof and an exterior wall off an adjacent building. Because the majority of the structural damage impacted older, less sturdy buildings, the tornado received a lower rating. Tornado is rated EF1 with max winds rated around 100 mph.

A tornado developed in the Via Caballero neighborhood in the south central portion of Santa Fe just north of I-25. The tornado traveled northward for approximately 1.4 miles, terminating near the College of Santa Fe. Much of the damage was along Rancho Siringo and Camino Chueco Roads. Damage included broken power poles, uprooted or damaged trees, damage to roofs. Ten homes sustained damaged. This tornado has been given a preliminary rating of EF-1, pending additional information.

A tornado developed south of I-25 with more impactful damage starting in the Via Caballero neighborhood in the south central portion of Santa Fe just north of I-25. The tornado traveled northward for approximately 2.25 miles, terminating near the College of Santa Fe. Much of the damage was along Rancho Siringo and Camino Chueco Roads. Damage included broken power poles, uprooted or damaged trees, damage to roofs. Ten homes sustained damaged with one home having the majority of the roof removed and a collapsed wall. This tornado has been given a rating of EF-1 with peak winds of 110 mph.

This tornado began near the intersection of Phillips Avenue and Ramsey Blvd. on the southwest end of Keyes. Here it snapped a few branches off of some elm trees and did damage to an older mobile home by pushing it a few feet, despite being anchored down. The tornado then continued northeast where it lifted an empty grain silo and either rolled or tossed or a combination of both across a field and landed about 100 yards or so to the northeast. It also snapped the top of a power pole. The tornado continued northeast  It caused some minor roof damage to the community center, including the collapse of one of the walls and destroyed the sidewalk awning connecting the two buildings. Another power pole was also broken in a couple of spots. This location likely had an enhancement of wind due to the enclosed nature of the area.
